text:
mike: heads-up, seeing a sudden cache-miss storm on kv-prefix for gptx-prod — hit-rate dropped ~85% -> 11% in the last 5m, backend QPS spiked ~9x. rolling back kernel-selector rollout? :eyes:

anya: confirmed in dashboards. per-model prefix hit-rate tanked exactly when kernel-selector-v2 was enabled for a subset of traffic. profiler shows key cardinality exploded.

sam: i think i know why — kernel-selector started including runtime kernel id in the cache key to avoid cross-kernel pollution. but the selector flips between kernels on micro-batching which creates high key entropy. bad interaction.

jess: emergency actions taken: disabled prefix-caching on affected pool (dedicated-us-west-2a) at 14:05 UTC; also throttled cache-write / fills globally. will monitor.

mike: thanks. after disable backend QPS dropped ~60% but tail latency still high for  p99. we should revert keying change asap and prewarm hot prefixes for top-200 prompts.

nima: attached profiler: kernel-selection adds ~1.2ms/token on critical path and — more importantly — we accidentally appended run metadata to prefix bytes when building the key. reproducer snippet: 

```python
# current (bad) key builder
key = sha256(f"{model}:{kernel}:{prefix_bytes}:{seq}")
# kernel fluctuates -> high cardinality

# desired key builder
canonical_key = sha256(f"{model}:{normalized_prefix}")
```

anya: proposed immediate mitigation: revert to canonical key (model + normalized_prefix) for cache lookups; keep kernel as metadata used for fallback routing only. add a cache-fill rate limit (50/s per model) to avoid stampedes.

sam: i can open a quick PR to gate kernel-in-key behind explicit model-config flag so default path excludes kernel. will include unit tests for deterministic keying.

jess: opened PR #2345 to normalize keying and add a prewarm job for top prompts. linked traces: https://observability.internal/redwood/trace/abcd. also added alert: cache-hit-rate < 50% sustained 2m.

infra-bot: deploy: rollback of config 'kernel-selector-v2' initiated by jess, deploy id kube-774. status: success.

mike: post-incident action items: 1) revert kernel-from-key until kernel-selector is stable; 2) add unit + integration tests for key canonicalization; 3) add synthetic warmup job that replays top-k prompts when kernel/config changes; 4) add alert for cache-fill QPS > baseline * 3; 5) doc the keying contract in eng-runtime docs.

anya: +1 on docs, i'll draft the keying contract and the warmup playbook. also recommend adding a short tokenized-prefix fingerprint vs raw-bytes check to avoid accidental metadata bleed.

mike: thanks everyone — follow-up sync in 30m. :thumbsup:
